desk.period: Q3 2026 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026; Paramount Skydance only, before the Warner Bros. Discovery deal closed)
desk.headline: Revenue up 5% to $7.0bn, in line; adjusted EPS beat; Warner Bros films to cut Q4 profit by up to $200m

other.label: Free cash flow
other.change: after $174m of restructuring and deal costs

results: Revenue rose 5% to $7.0bn, in line with forecasts; these figures exclude Warner Bros. Discovery, bought on 6 Oct.
Adjusted EPS was $0.45, well above the $0.20 expected; about $0.25 of that is a tax reserve the company excludes. GAAP EPS was $0.06.
Paramount+ revenue grew 21% (price rises and ads); Studios grew 23% on licensing, while TV Media fell 7% as pay-TV homes keep shrinking.
Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $1.0bn. Free cash flow was only $31m after restructuring and deal costs.
After the deal, gross debt is about $87bn with roughly $10bn of cash; spare cash beyond the dividend will go to paying down debt.

guidance.summary: Paramount on its own remains on track for its earlier 2026 guidance, at the $3.9bn top end for profit. For the combined company, Q4 film profit will be up to $200m lower because Warner Bros movies are underperforming. Full 2027 guidance comes with Q4 results; from then on guidance will be yearly.

items.new: mid-single-digit revenue growth, mid-20s% EBITDA margin, free cash flow over $10bn

points: Savings are front-loaded: about 30% of the $6bn target by end-2027 and 70% by end-2028, costing about $4bn in cash.
Possible revenue gains from the merger are left out of the plan; the $6bn target is cost savings only.
A Paramount+ and HBO Max bundle arrives in early 2027, with both on one tech platform in about a year; no price yet.
Management expects 2027 cash flow at break-even or better, including integration costs, and no need for asset sales.
Quarterly subscriber numbers will stop from Q4; an investor day is planned for the first half of 2027.
call.source: Shareholder letter (Exhibit 99) and call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 9 Nov 2026

watch: The first combined results and the 2027 outlook with Q4 numbers.
Progress on the $6bn savings plan and on paying down the $87bn of debt.
